quantification_note: Confirmed 2026-09-04 from the full text (Food Chem. 312:126082, PDF data/articles/trikusuma2020.pdf, section 2.5): 'Aroma compounds were quantified using a standard addition technique and DHS coupled with GC/MS-QQQ' (multiple reaction monitoring, 5-point standard addition curves, r2 > 0.960; 2-acetyl-1-pyrroline by SIDA). Dynamic headspace: the K_aw and HS-SPME bands apply.

Pea Protein Isolate.concentration_note: WITHDRAWN 2026-09-09. This field carried 1000 mM, which is not in the paper and cannot be: a protein isolate has no single molar mass. What the paper prints (Materials, and the beverage preparation) is a MASS FRACTION -- 'pea protein isolate (3 % w/w)', the isolate being 80 % protein, 8 % fat and 2 % sugar w/w -- which works out at about 2.4 % w/w protein and 0.24 % w/w fat (derived, trikusuma2020_extraction.md sec. 2). The row is scored on the matrix-only path, which reads the protein TYPE and not a molarity, so nothing that was scored depended on the withdrawn number; it is removed so that nothing later comes to depend on it.

vessel.provenance_note: Trikusuma, Paravisini & Peterson 2020, Food Chem. 312:126082, read from data/articles/trikusuma2020.pdf on 2026-09-04; this bundle's content_verification.quoted_conditions, verbatim: 'aseptic UHT processing ... processed at a final temperature and pressure of 140 C and 0.55 MPa for 6 s'. A UHT line is a continuous closed process with no fixed headspace (continuous_process); dissolved oxygen in the beverage is not reported. Water source for the 3 % w/w isolate beverage not stated.

conditions.water_activity_note: WITHDRAWN 2026-09-09. This field carried 0.98, which is a reasonable guess about a 3 % w/w aqueous dispersion and is not this paper's number: it prints no water activity, no moisture content and no dry-matter figure anywhere (trikusuma2020_extraction.md Flags 7).
conditions.carried_volatiles_anchor: Trikusuma, Paravisini & Peterson 2020 Table 2, the 'non-UHT processed' column, same table and same ug/L units as the 'UHT processed' column this bundle scores: hexanal 331 +/- 81.3, 2-pentylfuran 59.4 +/- 1.93, nonanal 8.24 +/- 0.44. The beverage as mixed, no heat. trikusuma2020_extraction.md sec. 3 Table 2. ADDED 2026-09-10 by wave B31: the panel had been scoring the heated column against a model that forms from zero, so 36 to 42 % of every measured level was raw material the model was being charged for. ||| WAVE B35 (2026-09-11): four more compounds from the SAME non-UHT column, on the same terms -- 2,5-dimethylpyrazine 2.46 +/- 0.12, methional 0.55 +/- 0.04, 2-acetyl-1-pyrroline 0.29 +/- 0.01, (E,E)-2,4-decadienal 0.06 +/- 0.005 ug/L. Declaring a carried level for three of the paper's seven compounds and not the other four would have been arbitrary.

content_verification_note.note: VALUES CONFIRMED against the open-access precursor of the paywalled paper: Trikusuma, M., MS thesis, The Ohio State University 2018, OhioLINK ETD accession osu1531495328317918, Table 6 p.35 — hexanal 781.72 +/- 58.59, 2-pentylfuran 163.16 +/- 15.06, nonanal 23.98 +/- 0.80 ug/L. The uncertainty_pct 8/9/4 recorded here match the SD-derived RSDs 7.5/9.2/3.3%. Conditions match (140 C, 6 s hold, pH 7.16 processed). WHICH COLUMN THIS IS, and it is load-bearing: these are the PROCESSED column. Table 6 also carries a Control column (331 / 59 / 8) and an AGED column (683 / 197 / 22) that differ materially; the process_metadata.state 'heated_matrix' label is what selects Processed and must not be re-read as either of the others. CITATION YEAR: the canonical citation is 2020 (Trikusuma, Paravisini & Peterson, Food Chemistry 312:126082), not 2019. The benchmark_id string 'Trikusuma2019' is retained UNCHANGED as an identifier only — it is referenced by data/lit/benchmark_intake_registry.json, src/matrix_calibration_registry.py, six test modules and every generated artifact, and renaming it would be an identity change, not a citation fix. Read the id as an opaque key; the year in it is wrong.
